findings.current: *Why? Cheongheoja hasn’t even launched a full assault. Why would he…?*
findings.defect: The draft makes Cheongheoja the one who has not launched an assault. The thought concerns the attackers’ decision not to press him.
findings.rationale: The observer is trying to explain why Cheongheoja would unleash Force when his own side has not deliberately mounted a fierce assault.
findings.replacement: *Why? We haven’t even pressed the attack. Why would Cheongheoja…?*
findings.source: ‘왜지? 일부러 맹공을 퍼붓지도 않았는데 청허자가 어째서.’

findings.current: A ghost horse, its white bones exposed, raced through the air like the wind, with several thousand fanatics charging behind it.
findings.defect: “Through the air” makes the horse appear to fly; the source describes its speed, not flight.
findings.rationale: 공간을 가로지르고 describes crossing the space ahead; nothing here says the horse leaves the ground.
findings.replacement: A ghost horse, its white bones exposed, raced forward like the wind, with several thousand fanatics charging behind it.
findings.source: 새하얀 뼈를 드러낸 유령마가 바람처럼 공간을 가로지르고

findings.current: A streak of light suddenly shot out, cutting through the middle-aged man’s neck along with the cloud of dust.
findings.defect: The draft omits the explicit identification of the middle-aged man as Hak Su.
findings.rationale: The narrator corrects “the middle-aged man” to “Hak Su” at the moment his neck is cut.
findings.replacement: A streak of light suddenly shot out, slicing through the dust cloud and the middle-aged man’s—no, Hak Su’s—neck.
findings.source: 불현듯 뻗어 나온 한 줄기의 섬광이 먼지구름과 함께 중년인의, 아니 학수의 목을 가로질렀다.

findings.current: The two jiangshi sorcerers had never seen these young men before. And there was also the bulky man who looked a little slow, and the strange fellow with wild hair.
findings.defect: “Young men” removes the women included in 연놈들.
findings.rationale: 연놈들 refers to young people of both sexes.
findings.replacement: The two jiangshi sorcerers had never seen these young men and women before. There was also a hulking man who looked none too bright, and a wild-haired eccentric.
findings.source: 처음 보는 젊은 연놈들에, 척 봐도 많이 모자라 보이는 것 같은 떡대와 산발의 괴인까지.

findings.current:
“Right. Taishan wants Pavilion Master. Also Old Man Nam.”

“Taishan. In a situation like this, you should say you miss them, not that you want them.”
findings.defect: “Wants” removes Taishan’s mistake: he says he wants to eat them when he means he misses them.
findings.rationale: The correction explicitly contrasts 먹고 싶다 (“want to eat”) with 보고 싶다 (“miss”).
findings.replacement:
“Right. Taishan wants to eat Pavilion Master. Old Man Nam, too.”

“Taishan. You mean you miss them, not that you want to eat them.”
findings.source:
“맞다. 태산이. 각주 먹고 싶다. 남 노인도.”

“태산아. 그럴 때는 먹고 싶다가 아니라 보고 싶다고 하는 것이다.”

findings.current: At the same time, the hill they had been standing on—or rather, the enormous masses of flesh hidden by the rain and confusion, which they could only have mistaken for a hill—answered the force.
findings.defect: “They could only have mistaken” attributes the mistake to the sorcerers commanding the masses.
findings.rationale: The source describes how the concealed masses appeared; it does not say the sorcerers themselves mistook them for a hill.
findings.replacement: At the same time, the hill they had been standing on—or rather, the enormous masses of flesh that the rain and chaos made impossible to distinguish from a hill—answered the force.
findings.source: 지금껏 그들이 서 있던 언덕이, 아니 빗줄기와 혼란에 가려져 언덕이라고 착각할 수밖에 없었던 거대한 살덩어리들이 그 강렬한 파장에 응답했다.

summary: The draft changes the subject of an attack, makes a galloping horse appear airborne, omits Hak Su’s reveal, and loses a character joke.
